headline: 140 kph gusts: Cyclone Arnab to hit India by Wednesday
summary: Andhra Pradesh and Odisha are preparing for the storm's landfall, with thousands of people being evacuated from vulnerable areas.
details: Cyclone Arnab, which formed over the Bay of Bengal, is expected to make landfall in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh by Wednesday morning.
According to India's weather office, the storm is expected to bring gusts of up to 140 kph (87 mph) and heavy to extremely heavy rainfall.
The rainfall is expected to impact Andhra Pradesh's northern and central coastal districts, as well as southern regions of neighboring Odisha.
Andhra Pradesh has identified 570,000 people as vulnerable and began evacuations on Monday evening, while ordering boats at sea to return to shore.
In Odisha, the government has closed schools and colleges in five districts for Tuesday and Wednesday as residents of low-lying areas are moved to cyclone shelters.
The Bay of Bengal remains one of the world's most active regions for tropical cyclones.
caption:
140 kph gusts and heavy rain: India is bracing for the landfall of Cyclone Arnab.

Cyclone Arnab, which formed over the Bay of Bengal, is expected to make landfall in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh by Wednesday morning.

According to India's weather office, the storm is expected to bring gusts of up to 140 kph (87 mph) and heavy to extremely heavy rainfall.

The rainfall is expected to impact Andhra Pradesh's northern and central coastal districts, as well as southern regions of neighboring Odisha.

Andhra Pradesh has identified 570,000 people as vulnerable and began evacuations on Monday evening, while ordering boats at sea to return to shore.

In Odisha, the government has closed schools and colleges in five districts for Tuesday and Wednesday as residents of low-lying areas are moved to cyclone shelters.

The Bay of Bengal remains one of the world's most active regions for tropical cyclones.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[reaches Tokyo on four-day official visit]] to Japan
headline: PM Tarique Rahman reaches Tokyo on four-day official visit to Japan
summary: The visit aims to deepen bilateral ties, attract fresh Japanese investment, and expand trade and development cooperation between the two nations.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived at Narita International Airport at 9:07 am local time, accompanied by his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and a small delegation.
The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold high-level bilateral talks with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on October 27, followed by a joint press announcement and a luncheon.
During the visit, he will meet with Japanese government officials, development institutions, and business leaders, and deliver a keynote address at the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum.
Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam stated that the visit is expected to attract fresh Japanese investment and accelerate ongoing development projects.
Discussions will focus on the implementation of the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) and expanding access for Bangladeshi products to the Japanese market.
The two nations will explore cooperation in renewable energy, agriculture, science and technology, digital transformation, and human resource development.
The Prime Minister's itinerary includes visits to an LNG terminal and power plant in Futtsu City, Chiba, the UNIQLO headquarters, and a Toyota factory in Nagoya.

Around eight Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) are under discussion, with three to four expected to be signed during the visit covering various sectors including civil aviation and environmental conservation.
The two sides will also discuss regional peace, a sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis, and cooperation in addressing the energy crisis.
Japan has been a major development partner of Bangladesh since 1972, supporting key projects like the Dhaka metro rail and the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
caption:
PM Tarique Rahman has arrived in Tokyo for a high-stakes four-day visit to strengthen trade, investment, and strategic ties with Japan.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived at Narita International Airport at 9:07 am local time, accompanied by his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and a small delegation.

The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold high-level bilateral talks with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on October 27, followed by a joint press announcement and a luncheon.

During the visit, he will meet with Japanese government officials, development institutions, and business leaders, and deliver a keynote address at the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum.

Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam stated that the visit is expected to attract fresh Japanese investment and accelerate ongoing development projects.

Discussions will focus on the implementation of the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) and expanding access for Bangladeshi products to the Japanese market.

The two nations will explore cooperation in renewable energy, agriculture, science and technology, digital transformation, and human resource development.

The Prime Minister's itinerary includes visits to an LNG terminal and power plant in Futtsu City, Chiba, the UNIQLO headquarters, and a Toyota factory in Nagoya.

Around eight Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) are under discussion, with three to four expected to be signed during the visit covering various sectors including civil aviation and environmental conservation.

The two sides will also discuss regional peace, a sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis, and cooperation in addressing the energy crisis.

Japan has been a major development partner of Bangladesh since 1972, supporting key projects like the Dhaka metro rail and the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
